subject: sociology
title: Theory & Methods: Positivism, Interpretivism & Realism
welcome_lead: Three philosophies of social science — how do we know society?
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology theory methods positivism interpretivism Bhaskar realism.

concepts.def: Comte — social facts measurable like nature.
Bhaskar — hidden structures cause observable patterns.
Layers of reality: empirical, actual, real.

walkthroughs.body_html: Comte (1842) founded sociology as natural science. Durkheim (1897) Suicide used social facts — Catholic countries had lower suicide rates than Protestant. Quantitative, value-free, generalisable. Modern surveys and statistics carry the legacy.

Weber (1922) argued humans differ from atoms — we attach meaning to action. Verstehen requires the researcher to grasp subjective meaning. Methods: unstructured interviews, participant observation. Mead and Blumer developed symbolic interactionism on this base.

Bhaskar (1975) argued reality has three layers: empirical (what we observe), actual (events whether observed or not), real (underlying structures generating events). Open systems explain why prediction in society is hard. Realism is now influential in sociology.
